issues.t: Backup camera goes blank or says unavailable (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse the center screen stays black, freezes, flickers, or shows a message that the camera is temporarily unavailable. Some owners also find the picture very dark at night.
issues.why: Software in the infotainment head unit can lose the video signal from the rear camera. Polestar issued three recalls for this (24V-477, then 25V-280, and finally 25V-615, which replaces the first two) because cars without a working rear view do not meet the federal rear-visibility rule. Many owners reported the problem came back after the first over-the-air fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN on the NHTSA or Polestar recall lookup and have the latest recall software installed for free, even if an earlier camera update was already done. Until it is fixed, look over your shoulder and use the mirrors when backing up.

issues.t: Center screen freezes, goes black or reboots
issues.sym: The touchscreen stops responding, goes black or restarts on its own. Sound can cut out, including turn-signal clicks and warning chimes, and climate or defrost controls may be unavailable until the system comes back.
issues.why: The Google-based infotainment system has software faults that can lock up the head unit. It is the most common fault owners report, and some cars needed more than one visit or software update before it settled down.
issues.next: Try a restart of the infotainment system (hold the home button until the screen reboots) and keep the car's software up to date. If it keeps happening, book a service visit; repairs have usually been covered under warranty.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains and car goes dead
issues.sym: The car won't wake up, unlock or shift into drive even though the big drive battery is charged. Screens may be dead or the car may act unresponsive.
issues.why: Like most EVs, the Polestar 2 uses a small 12-volt battery to power its computers, locks and screens. It is one of the most commonly reported faults, and a weak 12-volt battery can make the whole car seem dead.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and replaced if it is weak, and ask the dealer to check for software updates that reduce background drain. Keep a jump pack handy if the car sits for long periods.

issues.t: Propulsion system service required and loss of power
issues.sym: A 'Propulsion system service required' message appears, the car loses drive power or goes into a reduced-power limp mode, or it refuses to shift into drive for a while.
issues.why: Owners have reported sudden propulsion faults with warning lights. The exact cause varies; some cases were tied to battery or inverter software and were fixed with a dealer software update.
issues.next: If power is lost while driving, steer to a safe place and stop. Have the car towed or inspected rather than driving it on with the warning on, and make sure all recalls and software updates are done.

issues.t: Battery control module reset cuts drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The car can suddenly lose drive power while you are driving.
issues.why: The microprocessor in the battery energy control module could reset, which disconnects the high-voltage system. Polestar recall 21V-110 covers about 3,500 cars.
issues.next: Confirm the free software fix (done by a dealer or over the air) has been installed using your VIN.

issues.t: Connectivity module fails: no app, GPS or SOS
issues.sym: An 'eCall service required' message, no LTE connection, the phone app can't reach the car, GPS location is lost, and the emergency SOS button may not work. Phone-as-key and remote features can stop working.
issues.why: The telematics and connectivity antenna module (TCAM) that connects the car to the internet can fail, possibly from a bad batch of parts or software.
issues.next: Book a service visit. Many owners had the TCAM module replaced under warranty, which solved the problem. Remember emergency calling may not work until it is fixed.

issues.t: Car locks itself or won't recognize the key
issues.sym: The doors lock on their own or won't unlock with the key fob or phone key, the car may not recognize the key, or it won't let you shift into drive. In some cases the charging cable would not release.
issues.why: Faults in the car's electrical and connectivity systems, sometimes linked to a failed TCAM module or a 12-volt battery problem, can upset the keyless system. Owners say dealer resets don't always stop it coming back.
issues.next: Carry the physical key fob as a backup and never leave children or pets in the car alone. Have the dealer check the 12-volt battery, the TCAM module and software.

issues.t: Car brakes hard by itself when reversing or parking
issues.sym: While backing out of a driveway or into a garage the car slams on the brakes even though nothing is in the way.
issues.why: The rear automatic braking and cross-traffic braking features can be overly sensitive. Some owners noticed it more after a software update added auto braking.
issues.next: Learn where to turn off rear auto braking in the settings when you need to (it may reset each drive), and report false activations to the dealer so they can check sensors and software.

issues.t: Lane keeping or Pilot Assist steers unexpectedly
issues.sym: The lane-keeping system tugs the wheel toward a freeway exit or bike lane, or Pilot Assist does not stay centered in the lane.
issues.why: Driver-assistance complaints make up most owner reports for this car. Some owners noticed the behavior after over-the-air software updates.
issues.next: Keep your hands on the wheel at all times when these systems are on. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA, and turn lane keeping off if it keeps happening.

issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front of the car when braking or driving over bumps and rough roads.
issues.why: Owners have reported front-end knocking. Forum members point to the front strut top bearings, though the exact cause hasn't been confirmed by Polestar.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected, especially the strut mounts. If you're buying a used one, listen for it on the test drive and ask the seller to fix it first.

issues.t: Charging stops early or won't start
issues.sym: A DC fast-charging session stops partway and then fails at other chargers, or a scheduled-charging setting can't be turned off and blocks charging.
issues.why: Owners have reported charging software and settings glitches. Charging problems are a small share of complaints but can leave you stranded on a trip.
issues.next: Restart the car and try another charger. Check charging and schedule settings, keep the software updated and have the dealer read fault codes if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning before it fails. If the joint loosens you may feel looseness or hear a clunk from the front left, and in the worst case the control arm can separate from the steering knuckle and you lose steering control.
issues.why: On a very small number of 2023 cars the front left lower ball joint may not have been installed correctly at the factory (recall 23V-476).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer will inspect and replace the ball joint fastening bolt for free.

issues.t: Driver far-side airbag may not deploy right (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. An airbag warning light may appear on some cars.
issues.why: Clamps on the driver's inner far-side airbag module may not be crimped properly, so the airbag might not deploy as designed in a crash (recall 24V-939, a handful of 2024 cars).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer will replace the airbag module for free.
